newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Smooth polling in Malaysia's Sarawak state.
newsitem.headline: Smooth polling in Malaysia's Sarawak state.

text.p: Malaysian rainforest dwellers in traditional costume and smartly dressed city folk cast their ballots on Sunday in state assembly elections in the timber and oil-rich state of Sarawak.

The polling was staggered over two days, beginning Saturday, in the sprawling state on Borneo island to allow all eligible voters to cast their votes. Many of the state's population of 1.7 million live in dense rainforests in the interior.
Polling has been smooth so far with a steady stream of Sarawakians queueing up patiently, election officials said.

Political analysts expect no surprises in the election, with a coalition allied to Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's federal National Front expected to triumph, losing only a couple of seats at the most. The first results are expected as early as 1130 GMT, election officials said.
Some of the polling stations were set up at remote houses with election officials specially flown in.

Voters in the state capital of Kuching and other towns and cities travelled to polling stations by car, vans and buses while those in the interior used boats or trekked through jungle trails. Some voters wore tribal headdresses and other traditional costume.
Sarawak -- about as large as peninsular Malaysia itself -- -- is one of the poorest and least developed states in Malaysia, despite being rich in resources.
The state is populated by a dozen or so tribes, with the biggest represented in the governing coalition by their own parties.
Malaysia is the world's largest exporter of tropical timber and Sarawak accounts for nearly 80 percent of this.
Sarawak Chief Minister Abdul Taib Mahmud's National Front coalition got off to a strong start last month by winning 19 seats uncontested when candidates filed nomination papers.

Taib, who has headed the Sarawak government since 1981, controlled all 56 seats in the outgoing assembly, spread among four parties in his coalition. Another six seats have been added since the last election in 1991 to make a total of 62 seats.

A total of 109 candidates are contesting in 43 constituencies. They comprise 43 from the National Front, 60 independents and six from Malaysia's main opposition party, the Democratic Action Party (DAP).
